plot: On yard-sale morning the Dough Bros' dinner table is sold for twenty dollars; Bup insists it's just wood while Lolly wants to leave a goodbye, the bros sneak from a shoe box to under the table so Crispy can write 'D.B. Five' in soot, the buyer's van comes early and — the twist — tough Bup is the one who can't let go, hugging the notched leg where he first woke up and met Pim, until Lolly presses his crumb face into the notch so he can take it with him; the buyer keeps the writing, and then Dad hears the movers come Thursday, not Saturday.

beats.say: Bup! They're selling our table! Our actual table!
Calm down. It's just wood with legs.
Yard sale morning. Anything that isn't moving gets sold.
New episode every day. Subscribe so you don't miss what happens next.
That's where we have meetings! And snacks! And naps!
First no food in the truck. Now no table?!
Twenty dollars. The buyer comes back at noon with a van.
So we say goodbye. Fast. No crying. Moving on.
Bup keeps patting one table leg. The one with the notch.
Then we leave it something. A goodbye note.
Underneath. Where buyers never look. Nobody checks under tables.
I can write. With soot. Slowly.
One problem. The front lawn is full of people.
Neighbors. Strollers. A toddler grabbing anything small.
I'm small! I'm extremely small! I'm the smallest!
Five Dough Bros hide inside a box of old shoes.
Nobody breathe. These shoes smell like a gym.
Dad puts a lamp on the table. Then a fish tank.
We can't write under a fish tank! Physics says no!
Okay team. Under the table. Go, go, go!
They dash across the grass. A price sticker lands on Pim.
Why does my back say fifty cents?!
Because you're a bargain, sweetie. Keep running.
Fifty cents? He's worth at least a whole dollar!
Under the table it's dark and cool. Crispy starts writing.
D. B. Five. Dough Bros. All five.
Write bigger. So it lasts. So it really lasts.
Then a big white van rolls up to the curb. Early.
Faster, Crispy! The van door is opening!
Two big hands grab the tabletop. The table lifts.
Everybody out! Now! Let it go!
Four bros run out onto the grass. One doesn't.
Bup is hugging the table leg. Hugging it hard.
Bup! You said it's just wood!
I lied. I woke up right here. Behind this leg.
Stale. Alone. Then a red bean said hello.
Th-that was me. I was so scared of you.
That notch is my first day. I can't leave it.
The table rises. Bup's little feet leave the grass.
Then don't leave it. Take it with you. Like this.
Lolly presses Bup's face to the notch. A crumb print stays.
Now you're in the table. And the table's in you.
Bup lets go. He drops into a pile of four friends.
Okay. Goodbye, table. Thanks for everything.
The buyer tips the table into the van. Then he stops.
Under the top, in soot: D.B. Five. And a tiny crumb face.
He's going to wipe it off. I just know it.
He doesn't. He smiles, and slides it in very carefully.
Good table. Good man. I didn't hate that.
Then Dad's phone rings. He listens. His face drops.
'The movers come Thursday. Not Saturday. This Thursday.'
What do you think happens in the next part?
Tell me in the comments.
